mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.1%) indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.1%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate exceeding 4.0% indicates a deteriorating labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 4.0, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals a broad-based weakening of consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle slowdown regime characterized by declining industrial production (INDPRO), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns as investors anticipate reduced corporate profits from weak manufacturing activity over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO declines and the regime is classified as late-cycle slowdown, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1600 thousand units signals strong consumer demand for housing, which boosts related sectors and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when HOUST > 1600, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and year-over-year CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicates a tightening monetary policy in response to high inflation, which compresses equity valuations and causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of periods when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL rise, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a strong labor market regime characterized by monthly nonfarm payrolls growth exceeding 100,000 jobs, the S&P 500 experiences positive forward returns as consumer spending and corporate earnings are supported over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS growth > 100, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production index below 100 (2017=100) signals a contraction in manufacturing activity that reduces corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 100, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
